protocol.query_rule: Each query is paraphrased only from the linked upstream issue behavior before inspecting the fix, target source file, target symbol, containing class/type/module, or qualified identity. Queries must not contain those answer identities or distinctive implementation literals. After this file is committed, ground-truth lookup is permitted, but the query text is immutable.
protocol.note: This is the pre-ground-truth query freeze. It intentionally contains no expected files or symbols. The commit containing this file is the audit boundary after which answer lookup may begin.

tasks.query: HTTP connection-close tokens should be interpreted case-insensitively, including comma-separated values, so the server closes the connection and reflects the close directive.
A WebSocket handshake denial response must not add duplicate content type or content length headers when the application already supplied them.
Hot-reload restart and shutdown must not block forever waiting for workers that keep long-lived streaming or WebSocket connections open.
Forwarded client addresses that already contain a port must be parsed without appending a second zero port or corrupting host and port information.
A positioned read that returns fewer bytes than requested must also return a non-null error explaining why the buffer was not completely filled.
Renaming an in-memory directory must move its children so files remain reachable beneath the new directory name.
Truncating an in-memory file to zero must keep the write position consistent so the next write does not insert a run of zero bytes first.
Reading directory entries with a non-positive count must return all remaining entries in one result rather than applying the positive-count paging behavior.
When overlapping alternatives can both match, the search must return the earliest leftmost match rather than a later suffix match.
A search combining a negated character class with an optional parenthesized group must preserve leftmost-match semantics instead of starting inside the parentheses.
Searching capture slots must not panic when a capture group is repeated zero times, even if the caller provides more slot capacity than the pattern will populate.
When byte-oriented matching is configured to honor Unicode, iteration over empty matches must advance on Unicode character boundaries rather than every raw UTF-8 byte.
A successfully completed asynchronous operation with a null value must still be recorded as a success rather than disappearing from success metrics.
If the predicate used to decide whether an asynchronous failure should be retried throws, the returned promise must complete exceptionally instead of hanging forever.
When retry scheduling is stopped by a negative delay after an operation fails, callers should receive the original failure rather than a null-pointer error.
Concurrent cache misses for the same key should coordinate so the underlying computation runs once and other callers share the result.
Responses whose status forbids a body must not retain chunked transfer encoding merely because trailers were registered.
Graceful shutdown of an HTTP/2 server must close active sessions instead of only refusing new sessions and waiting indefinitely.
An injected test request must not enter unbounded memory growth when a streamed response fails after headers and some body data have already been sent.
When a response is explicitly marked as JSON, sending a string value should serialize it as JSON rather than writing the raw string unchanged.
On Windows, arguments ending in one or more quote characters must survive parsing instead of being unconditionally trimmed.
An action attached directly to an option must propagate its integer result instead of silently discarding the returned exit code.
An option-level action must still run when its parent command has no action of its own.
After a caller clears a previously assigned custom argument parser, parsing must fall back to the default converter instead of continuing to call the old parser.
